name: Question 5
problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-4x{y}^{′}+6y=-6x+1,\,x>0
$$

has the complimentary function ${y}_{c}(x)=A{x}^{2}+B{x}^{3}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation.
worked_solution:
The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $-6x+1.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is of the form 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\alpha x+\beta ,
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are the constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=\alpha ,\,\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}=0.
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation and group the terms on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}(0)-4x(\alpha )+6(\alpha x+\beta ) & =-6x+1 \\ (-4\alpha +6\alpha )x+6\beta  & =-6x+1 \\ 2\alpha x+6\beta  & =-6x+1\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2\alpha =-6\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\,x) \\ 6\beta =1\, & (\text{equating the constants})\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =-3$ and $\beta =\frac{1}{6}.$

Hence, the particular integral ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=-3x+\frac{1}{6}.
$$

Question 5

Given that the differential equation

x2y″−4xy′+6y=−6x+1,x>0

has the complimentary function yc(x)=Ax2+Bx3, find the particular solution yp(x) to this equation.

a
yp(x)=−4x+1
b
yp(x)=6x−2
c
yp(x)=−3x+16
d
yp(x)=12x+23
e
yp(x)=−13x+5
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is −6x+1. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is of the form

yp(x)=αx+β,

where α and β are the constants that are to be determined.

Calculating the first and second derivatives of yp gives

dypdx=α,d2ypdx2=0.

To find the values of α and β, we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation and group the terms on the left-hand side:

x2(0)−4x(α)+6(αx+β)=−6x+1(−4α+6α)x+6β=−6x+12αx+6β=−6x+1

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

{2α=−6(equating the coefficients ofx)6β=1(equating the constants)

Solving this system gives α=−3 and β=16.

Hence, the particular integral yp(x) is

yp(x)=−3x+16.
